title: Wirex Adds Tokenized US Stocks to Its Infrastructure and Wirex One App
description: Wirex says partners can integrate tokenized US equities through its API and SDK, while eligible Wirex One users can access Base-based tokens without underlying shareholder rights.
why_it_matters: The rollout offers a distribution channel for tokenized equity exposure through a consumer app and partner infrastructure, but the tokens are not equivalent to directly owning company shares. Eligibility limits and missing voting rights are central distinctions for assessing this RWA product.
keyTakeaways: Wirex announced tokenized US stock access for eligible Wirex One customers and infrastructure partners on November 17.
The company says the tokens are built on Base and issued by Coinbase, with Apple, Amazon and Microsoft among the examples.
Partners can integrate access through Wirex Infrastructure's API and SDK.
Wirex explicitly warns that the tokens do not grant ownership of underlying shares or voting rights.
body:
Wirex announced on November 17 that tokenized exposure to US stocks is available through its infrastructure platform and the Wirex One application. The company says eligible customers can buy and hold blockchain-based tokens referencing shares such as Apple, Amazon and Microsoft, with around-the-clock access rather than conventional exchange trading hours.

According to the company's release, the tokens operate on the Base network and are issued by Coinbase. Wirex describes them as backed one-for-one by shares, although that claim is made by the issuer's distribution partner and does not itself establish independent reserve verification. Wirex also offers the product to businesses through its existing infrastructure API and software development kit, allowing partners to integrate access into their own applications.

Wirex says its Wirex One app is the first deployment of the offering and refers to nearly two million users. That figure describes the app's stated audience, not confirmed tokenized-stock holders or trading activity. Availability depends on jurisdiction and eligibility.

Crucially, the company's disclaimer says these products do not transfer legal ownership of the underlying shares or shareholder rights, including voting. The announcement therefore marks a new distribution option for tokenized market exposure, not a replacement for directly holding listed equities.

facts.claim: Wirex announced tokenized stock availability for eligible partners and Wirex One users on November 17.
The company says tokenized stocks are built on the Base network and issued by Coinbase.
The announced tokenized stock examples include Apple, Amazon and Microsoft shares.
Wirex says partner integration is available through its infrastructure API and SDK.
facts.anchor: single Wirex Infrastructure API and SDK

facts.claim: The release states that token holders receive neither underlying legal share ownership nor shareholder voting rights.
